2.

sentences.text: The appellant/claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.42,00,000/- by the dependents of the deceased Balakrishnan @ Pandi, who sustained fatal injuries in a motor accident on 27.01.2018.

3. The learned Tribunal after hearing both sides and upon considering the oral and documentary evidence has granted compensation Rs.17, 73, 200/- in the following manner:-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 29/07/2025 07:43:07 pm ) Sl.No Description

Amount awarded by Tribunal 1. Totall loss of dependency Rs.16,63,200/-
2. Loss of Consortium Rs.80,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-
Total Rs.17, 73,200/-
4.

The Tribunal directed the above compensation to be paid by the 2nd respondent with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a.
5.
The appellant/claimant, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal,, has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the accident was happened in the year 2018 but the Tribunal without considering the cost of living in the year,
passed the award as such is erroneous one.

He further submitted that the award passed by the Tribunal under all the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
29/07/2025 07:43:07 pm ) heads is lower, which requires interference by this Court S.Mookkan vs G.Usha on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158617956/
2 and prays to allow this appeal.

7. The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal taking into consideration all the relevant documents has rightly fixed the compensation, which does not require any interference.
Hence, he prayed for dismissal of this appeal.
8. In the instant case, the accident was happened in the year 2018, considering the cost of living at that time of accident 2018, this Court is enhanced the monthly income of Rs.16,000/-.
Further, enhanced the loss of dependency (16000+40%=22400x12x18x1/2=24,19,200).
In other aspects, the amount awarded by the Tribunal appears to be reasonable.

Therefore, the Compensation award by the Tribunal is reworked as tabulated below:-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Sl.N Description Amount Amount Award o awarded by awarded by confirmed Tribunal this Court or enhanced 1.
Totall
loss of Rs.16,63,200/- Rs.24,19,200/- enhanced dependency 2. Loss of Consortium Rs.80,000/- Rs.80,000/- confirmed 3. Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/- confirmed

4. Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/- confirmed Total Rs.17,73,200/-
Rs.25,29,200/-
9.

In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed in part and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.17,73,200/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.25,29,200/- together with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of deposit.

The 2nd respondent is directed to deposit the entire award amount now determined by this Court along with interest, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment, to the credit of MCOP.No.1354 of 2018 on the file of the Special Sub Court-II, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, (Court of Small Causes, Chennai)
